stories.title: Dhaka University maintains admission schedule despite UGC request
stories.summary: Dhaka University will proceed with its admission tests according to its previously announced schedule, rejecting a request from the University Grants Commission to defer the dates. The university confirmed the application deadline remains November 25, effectively excluding students waiting on results from upcoming supplementary examinations.

stories.title: JEE Main 2027 registration numbers expected to reach 17 lakhs
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency is expected to report between 16 and 17 million registrations for the upcoming JEE Main 2027 session. The final date for submission is November 22, 2027, with exams scheduled to begin in January. The agency has not yet released the official final count.

stories.title: Dhaka University rejects coordinated admission schedule
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission has decided to move public university admission tests to February, but Dhaka University will continue with its own timeline. The university has also relaxed some departmental admission requirements while maintaining its original application schedule. The university remains committed to its own calendar.

stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has introduced a registration option for NRI candidates applying for JEE Main 2027 without an Aadhaar card. Applicants with a valid Indian passport may now use the designated portal option to complete their registration. The agency is providing alternative verification for non-residents.

stories.title: Dhaka University declines UGC request to delay admissions
stories.summary: Dhaka University has rejected a call from the University Grants Commission to reconsider its admission schedule in the interest of students. The university will maintain its original timeline, meaning students awaiting supplementary exam results will be unable to apply. The university has chosen its own path.

stories.title: Dhaka University confirms admission tests will proceed as planned
stories.summary: Dhaka University will hold its undergraduate admission tests for the 2026-27 session as scheduled, despite a request from the University Grants Commission to defer. Pro-Vice-Chancellor Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane confirmed the decision, noting that while students awaiting re-evaluation may sit for tests, those who failed will not be accommodated.

stories.title: Dhaka University maintains admission timeline
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission has requested that public universities defer admission tests to accommodate students awaiting supplementary exam results. Dhaka University has decided to ignore the request and will stick to its original schedule. The university finalised these dates in August and expects to proceed accordingly.

stories.title: Cambridge report questions security of remote English testing
stories.summary: A recent paper from Cambridge University Press and Assessment warns against accepting at-home English tests for visa applications until security measures are improved. The report suggests that remote testing, while increasingly mainstream, lacks the oversight of traditional centres. It questions if such tests are truly fit for purpose.

stories.title: Canada cuts, NZ grows as Australia and US rethink international education
stories.summary: International education’s most established destinations are no longer following the same script. stories.title: UK business schools report decline in international enrolments
stories.summary: The Chartered Association of Business Schools reports that 69 percent of member schools saw a drop in international enrolments this year. With most schools relying on these fees for financial viability, the decline in postgraduate recruitment is described as a serious concern. The sector is feeling the impact.

stories.summary: AIEC 2026: International students and graduates on life in Australia At The PIE’s international student roundtable at the Australian International Education Conference (AIEC) 2026, international students and graduates shared their experiences in Australia, the challenges they face, their aspirations and ideas for change. stories.title: UK transitions visa holders to digital eVisas
stories.summary: The United Kingdom is moving from physical immigration documents to digital records. Visa holders, including Nigerians, are now required to create a UKVI account to verify their identity and link their status to an eVisa. The government has released a pictorial guide to assist with the process.

stories.title: Democratic majorities face legislative hurdles
stories.summary: Incoming Democratic majorities in the US Congress plan to investigate President Trump and hold immigration agencies accountable. While the party holds new legislative power, Trump retains the presidential veto. The president has frequently reminded the public of his ability to stifle legislation he opposes.

stories.title: Boston University objects to proposed OPT fee
stories.summary: Boston University President Melissa Gilliam and Provost Colin Duckett have formally objected to a proposed $70,000 fee for international students using the federal Optional Practical Training program. The university warns the cost would shrink student numbers, harming both the institution and Massachusetts employers.

stories.title: Failed visa applications cost Nigerians billions
stories.summary: Nigerian families lose over N75 billion annually to failed migration attempts, according to new findings. Each unsuccessful visa application costs approximately N1.2 million in fees and documentation. Many families sell property or borrow money to fund these attempts, only to face high rejection rates abroad.

stories.title: Visa rule changes force resident to leave Australia
stories.summary: A British woman has been forced to leave Australia after a visa rule change disrupted her plans for further study. The resident, who spent three years on the Gold Coast, faced significant costs and uncertainty following the government's recent shift in migration policy. The policy remains in flux.

stories.title: UTEP announces engineering scholarship with bonus
stories.summary: The University of Texas at El Paso has opened applications for the Loya Scholarship. The program covers tuition, housing, food, and transportation for engineering students, while providing a $1,000 monthly stipend. Graduates will also receive a $30,000 bonus upon completion of their degree.

stories.title: Meeting Street Scholarship expands in South Carolina
stories.summary: The Meeting Street Scholarship Fund has opened applications for the 2027-28 academic year, now available to students in all 46 South Carolina counties. The fund offers up to $10,000 for college to students with demonstrated financial need. A new online application aims to remove barriers for applicants.

stories.title: LLCC Foundation scholarship applications
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. The LLCC Foundation 2026-27 scholarship application portal is currently experiencing technical errors and is unavailable for access at this time. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Alberta Blue Cross Indigenous scholarship program
stories.summary: Alberta Blue Cross is accepting applications for its Indigenous scholarship program, which awards 12 students $1,500 each. The program is open to full-time students in accredited post-secondary courses of at least two years. Last year, the organization received nearly 240 applications from across the province.

stories.title: Corvias Foundation opens two scholarship programs
stories.summary: The Corvias Foundation has opened applications for two college scholarships. The Purple Tassel program supports military-connected high school seniors, while the Family Scholarship is available to children of Corvias employees. Both programs provide funding for four-year degrees to eligible students.

stories.title: NFL star funds scholarships for Florida students
stories.summary: Khalil Mack and his wife have launched a scholarship program awarding $5,200 to 52 Florida students. The Khalil Mack 52 Scholars Program is open to African-American high school seniors and undergraduates with a 3.0 GPA or higher. The foundation committed $270,400 to the initiative.

stories.title: Cecil College scholarship applications now open
stories.summary: Cecil College has opened scholarship applications for the 2027-28 academic year. Awards range from $100 to full tuition and fees. Last year, the foundation awarded approximately $487,633 to 345 students, with individual awards averaging about $1,413. The application period closes on April 30, 2027.

stories.title: UK scholarships for Bangladeshis
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Fully funded UK scholarships for Bangladeshi students are scheduled to open for applications tomorrow. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: China offers scholarships to Kenyan students
stories.summary: The Chinese government has announced 15 fully-funded scholarships for Kenyan students for the 2027/2028 academic year. The awards cover undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral programs. The Ministry of Education in Nairobi will serve as the exclusive authority for managing the application process.

stories.title: Postgraduate scholarship opportunities for Nigerians
stories.summary: Nigerian graduates seeking to study abroad in 2027 have access to various scholarship programs in the UK and France. Funding levels vary, with some institutions offering full tuition and living expenses while others provide partial fee reductions. Applicants are advised to verify coverage details carefully.

stories.title: Kenya announces Chinese government scholarships
stories.summary: Kenya’s Ministry of Education has confirmed that China is offering government scholarships for undergraduate, master’s, and PhD studies during the 2027/2028 academic year. Eligible Kenyan applicants can apply through the ministry, which is coordinating the process following communication from the Chinese Embassy in Nairobi.

stories.title: Post-matric scholarship information
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. The requested information regarding the 2026-27 post-matric scholarship list and eligibility criteria is currently inaccessible due to a server error. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Toxic haze disrupts university life in South-east Asia
stories.summary: Forest fires in Indonesia have blanketed the region in a tangerine haze, forcing universities to suspend face-to-face learning and limit outdoor activities. While the environmental risks are growing, there is little confidence that institutions have established plans to manage future crises. The air remains thick.

stories.title: Widening participation progress slipping away amid cuts
stories.summary: UK universities face their most difficult position in decades as budget cuts and anti-university rhetoric squeeze access programmes. The Office for Students is currently scrapping the Uni Connect scheme to replace it with a new regional programme. Access remains a priority, according to ministers.

stories.title: GAU secures 2nd place in world university rankings
stories.summary: Gazipur Agricultural University has secured second place among Bangladeshi institutions in the QS World University Asia Rankings 2027 for research papers per faculty. With a score of 61.8 on the index, the university has consolidated its position as a top research-based institution in the country.

stories.title: Illinois university named top college in the Midwest by Forbes
stories.summary: Northwestern University has been named the best college in the Midwest by Forbes, citing its journalism school and the number of alumni on the publication's leadership list. The University of Michigan Ann Arbor took third place, highlighted for its return on investment for graduates.

stories.title: Boston University misses revenue projections by $42M
stories.summary: Boston University missed its revenue projections by $42 million. The private institution will now need to change on a much broader scale rather than relying on one-time budget cuts, according to its chief financial officer. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: UNO ranked No. 5 school in the nation for veterans
stories.summary: The University of Nebraska at Omaha has been ranked fifth out of 370 universities in the 2026 Best for Vets: College Rankings by Military Times. The institution is recognized for supporting military-connected students and veterans through both in-person and online education programmes.

stories.title: ASU ranks second among public universities for graduate employability
stories.summary: Arizona State University has been ranked second among public universities for graduate employability. The ranking was published by The Business Journals. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: University of Washington, Seattle
stories.summary: Founded in 1861, the University of Washington is a public research institution with an undergraduate population of 40,684. The total annual cost is $65,541, with an average grant aid of $16,156. The median salary for alumni with 10 years of experience is $116,327.

stories.title: Penn State faces $124M budget hole
stories.summary: Penn State faces a $124 million budget deficit following a decline of roughly 3,060 students. Officials attributed half of the enrollment drop to the closure of seven Commonwealth Campuses. The university is now working to address the shortfall across its remaining campuses and programmes.

stories.title: UCSB makes a strong showing in annual college rankings
stories.summary: UC Santa Barbara continues to place highly in prominent rankings for research, academics and value. Chancellor Dennis Assanis stated that the university is driven by the relentless pursuit of excellence, noting that the assessments serve as a testament to the institution's culture of innovation.

stories.title: Sri Lankan university rankings continue to fall
stories.summary: The University of Colombo has fallen to 364th in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027, down from 275th two years ago. While countries with similar or lower incomes have seen their institutions rise, Sri Lankan universities continue to sit far below regional peers.

stories.title: Specialist business school courses under threat
stories.summary: Business schools are preparing to make strategic decisions about their course portfolios in a difficult economic environment. Ulster University Business School dean Gillian Armstrong noted that smaller programmes may be cut, even if businesses value them, as schools struggle to manage their complex offerings.

stories.title: Stony Brook University tracks community engagement
stories.summary: Stony Brook University has launched a tracking effort to monitor community engagement from Montauk to Manhattan. The university welcomes about 4,000 students from more than 100 countries annually, providing resources through its International Student Success office to help students navigate life far from home.

stories.title: Understanding proposed changes to OPT
stories.summary: The American Physical Society has published information regarding proposed changes to the Optional Practical Training programme for international students. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: New branch campuses make stuttering start in India
stories.summary: Western universities opening branch campuses in India have seen muted interest, with some institutions attracting only a few dozen students. An analysis found median inaugural enrollments of 120 per campus. The branch campuses are located in a greenfield precinct designed for foreign entities.

stories.title: Interdisciplinary research is recognised but not rewarded
stories.summary: Universities increasingly value interdisciplinary research, yet promotion systems often remain focused on single-disciplinary achievement. A report from the Global Higher Education Interdisciplinary Network found that while some institutions are reforming these systems, obstacles to rewarding cross-cutting work remain in place at many universities.

stories.title: Official Secrets Act invoked in NCRA exam leak case
stories.summary: A staffer at the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics has been booked under the Official Secrets Act for allegedly leaking a recruitment exam paper. The vigilance department received a tip-off regarding the breach, which reportedly involved the distribution of the paper via WhatsApp.

stories.title: NTA reforms exam security following leaks
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency is overhauling its security by creating a large question bank and preparing papers hours before tests. The plan, led by a committee under Nandan Nilekani, also involves using retired army officers to supervise centers to prevent future leaks.

stories.title: North-West University hosts international teaching week
stories.summary: North-West University hosted an International Teaching Week to provide students with global perspectives and diverse teaching approaches. The programme brought together delegates from six countries for academic exchange and collaboration. The initiative was organised under the University Capacity Development Programme to broaden understanding of global higher education.

stories.title: Photo series: Friends of international students pumpkin carving
stories.summary: The Scarlet and Black published a photo series documenting a pumpkin carving event for international students held on November 9, 2026. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Bath Taps into Science festival returns to the city
stories.summary: The University of Bath is hosting its free two-day science festival this week, featuring experiments and hands-on activities for schools and families. The event aims to connect the public with researchers and science professionals. The festival requires no booking for the Saturday family day.

stories.title: Keralam government eases rules for autonomous college courses
stories.summary: The government has relaxed requirements for prior approval to introduce self-financing courses and increase seats in autonomous colleges. The Opposition claims this facilitates commercialisation, while the government cites academic autonomy and reduced bureaucracy. The Higher Education Department issued the revised circular on November 6.

stories.title: Connecting trigonometry to the real world
stories.summary: Maths teachers frequently face questions about the practical utility of trigonometry. While students often rely on memory tricks like SOH-CAH-TOA and calculators to solve problems, the subject offers a method for measuring the unseen. The challenge remains in connecting abstract formulae to observable reality.

stories.title: International students find community through affinity groups
stories.summary: International students at Northwestern are using affinity groups and shared interests to build community on campus. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many societal decisions are settled by contests of persuasion. Conversational AI is a powerful new entrant in these contests, but whether it can out-persuade skilled and highly incentivized humans has remained unclear. Here, in a series. research.title: AI ‘slop’ is a social judgement
research.summary: Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 09 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02639-6 Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content increasingly saturates our information environment. Efforts to detect and remove it are failing. We propose that calling AI-generated content ‘slop’ is best understood as a social judgement: what a community recognizes as unwanted AI content.
